lines.en: label mayafestival2:
Maya and I leave the house together and begin to make our way to a festival at-
: Wait, where is this festival exactly?
: Far away.
: Well, as far as we can go within the confines of Kumon-mi, that is.
: There’s one closer, but I didn’t want to risk the chance of someone seeing me with you in public and thinking we like each other.
: We do like each other, though.
: No. You like me. It’s different.
: Don’t worry too much about where it is as there’s not much reason to ever go back.
: The surrounding areas have mostly closed down anyway since the school building there is no longer in use.
: Are we taking the bus, then?
: Partly. We’ll have to walk for about half an hour after we get off since the bus doesn’t stop where we’re actually headed anymore.
: The more I hear about this place, the more I think this is some elaborate ploy for you to kill me.
: There are much easier ways for me to kill you.
: But in the event that I am just looking for a challenge, you should at least thank me first for allowing you to see me in my yukata in your final moments.
: Oh well. I’ve had a good run.
Anyway, we leave the house together and begin to make our way to a festival at some undisclosed location far away from my house that buses pretend doesn’t exist for some reason.
It’s confusing, yes. But so is literally everything about this city and I am tired of trying to attribute meaning to any of it.
And, like Maya says, there’s no reason for me to ever go back. So I might as well just stop thinking about it and try to enjoy the rest of the day with her.
If we ever make it there, that is.
At this rate, I-
scene smileex
scene tree3
scene mayafestival1
: Oh. We’re here.
A swarm of lights surrounds us, both natural and artificial, and the scents of various street foods assault my senses.

I still haven’t eaten anything on account of Maya claiming my breakfast as her own, so I’m starting to get a little hungry and hope that my companion here doesn’t empty my bank account out on herself.
Upon closer observation, I can tell this is somewhere I haven’t been before.
But, like many things, it feels familiar.
Even Maya’s presence feels familiar, so...maybe this is somewhere we’ve gone together in the past?
: Hey. If buses don’t come here and there’s no reason to ever visit this part of town, how do you know about it?
: I know every nook and cranny of Kumon-mi. I just choose to avoid most of them.
: Have we ever come here together before?
: I’m not going to answer that. If you trick me into allowing you to commit suicide-by-memory on my birthday, I will never forgive you.
: This place just feels a little familiar. That’s all.
: Perhaps it is, then.
scene mayafestival2
: Anyway, I’ll be taking your credit card now.
: Fine. I will be taking your credit card, please.
: Give me your fucking credit card. I’m hungry.
: Do they even take credit cards here? This place seems pretty traditional.
: ATMs exist, you know. Just give me the card.
: This doesn’t sound very much like “spending time together.”
: Do you see how many stalls there are here? We’ll never be able to hit all of them if we stick together.
: This festival has two halves. I need you to handle all of the stalls on the west side while I handle all of the ones on the east.
: Card. Now. Give.
: At least tell me what you want me to order for you first.
: Yes.
: Not really a yes or no question, Maya.
: You see, that is where you are wrong.
: You never wanted me here at all, did you? I’m just the only person you know with a credit card.
scene mayafestival3
: If I say no and promise to...catch goldfish with you or something once I’m done eating, will you give it to me?
: I don’t have the time to take care of a goldfish.
: It’s a goldfish. You put it in water. That’s literally it.
: I feel like you’re supposed to feed it occasionally too.
scene mayafestival4
: Why do you care more about feeding your hypothetical goldfish than me? I am much more attractive and fun to be around.
: Attractive, sure. But I think you might be overestimating how fun you are.
: I think you might be overestimating how fun a goldfish is. Card, please.
: This is not a joke. We have already wasted far too much time.
: Fine. But at least tell me where the two of us are supposed to meet back up. I don’t want to risk losing you in this crowd.
scene mayafestival5
: There’s a gazebo near the entrance with some picnic tables. Just meet me there.
: Also, what crowd? There’s barely anyone here yet.
: And “getting separated at the festival” is far too tropey for real life when we both know that any drama to spring up today will be from you saying or doing something disgusting.
: Sure hope I don’t accidentally get anyone pregnant while buying your lunch.
scene mayafestival6
: Have I ever told you how much I hate you?
: Plenty of times.
: Just making sure.
scene black
I give Maya one of my credit cards and thank whoever I was in the past for being responsible enough to carry two of them.
Her ponytail bounces up and down as she runs off and, honestly, it’s probably the most active I’ve ever seen her apart from a few fantasies I don’t want to tell you about.
I stop in my tracks for a moment and observe my surroundings one more time before going in the opposite direction of Maya when I realize something.
I don’t think we’re in the old district right now.
But...
I don’t think we’re in the new one either?
Where is this place?
: You there!
: You look like the kinda guy who could use a nice pair of melons!
scene mayafestival7
: We’ve got normal melons! We’ve got square melons! We’ve got triangle melons! Any kinda melon you can dream of!
: So long as it’s one of those three shapes. Anything else, you’re gonna have to join the waitlist for.
if sarasex == True:
: Wait...I’ve seen you before.
scene mayafestival8
: Oh?
: Yeah. Didn’t we bump into each other in the middle of the night once or something?
: Hmm...yeah! You were the guy with the phone!
: That isn’t exactly how I would describe myself, but yes. I was the guy with the phone.
: Glad to see you made it back in one piece.
: And I’m glad to see you’re a...melon salesperson.
: Oh, this? This is just a temporary thing.
: I don’t even really like fruit.
: Well, you have chosen a very peculiar line of work then.
else:
: What other shapes would they even come in?
: Beats me. But if you join the waitlist, you can probably find out.
: So, is it melon time? Or is it not melon time? I’ve got a very limited supply, you know.
: It is most certainly “melon time,” but I think I should ask you to confirm the quality of said melons since the girl I’m here with today is a bit of a connoisseur.
: Wanna give ‘em a squeeze and find out?
: That depends on whether or not the police will get involved.
scene mayafestival9
: Ahh, we’ve got a pervert on our hands! That’s great! I’ve worked with you types before.
: There are a lot of us in the melon trade.
: You know what? For today and today only, I’ll throw in a second melon half-off. One for the two of you to share.
: If she even wants to share, that is. As a melon connoisseur myself, I understand how tough it can be to share what you love with other people!
: How much are they?
scene mayafestival10
: They’re...uhh...
: You don’t know the price of your own products?
scene mayafestival11
: Six million!
: Yen?
: Pesos!
: I don’t think I have any of those on me.
: How does 500 yen sound?
scene mayafestival12
: 500? That’s it? These melons are easily worth double that. I think. Probably.
: This is my first day on the job, so I’m not really sure. But that also means you have to be nice to me since I’m nervous and my feelings are easily hurt.
: Then...1,000 yen for two melons. Post discount.
scene mayafestival13
: Deal! Would you like these gift wrapped? I’ll do it myself for...oh, I don’t know...an extra six million pesos?
: You seem dead set on that specific number and...currency. Mind if I ask why?
: A magician never reveals her secrets!
: You’re a magician now?
: And an astronaut!
: But right now, melons matter most!
: I’m going to say no to the gift wrapping, but I wouldn’t mind getting your name.
scene mayafestival14
: My name? Why?
: Are you flirting with me? Does the sale hinge on this?
: No. It’s just to satisfy my own curiosity.
scene mayafestival15
: My name, huh...
: Is there a problem with that?
: It’s just that nobody’s ever asked me before.
: I find it hard to believe that no one’s ever asked you for your name.
: Hey, you can believe whatever you want to believe. You don’t have to pick up all the stuff I put down, Mr. Pervert.
: Please don’t call me that.
: Nope. That’s your name now. You have to live with it.
: This is the part where you tell me yours.
scene mayafestival8
: Nope! This is the part where I don’t tell you and you still buy my melons anyway!
: Can I at least have the first letter?
: Nope! All I’ll tell you is that it’s really funny.
: Your name is?
: Hilarious. A real kick to the shin.
: Then I apologize for how much you likely get made fun of in school.
scene mayafestival16
: Who says I go to school?
: You don’t? I just thought you looked a little young.
: Oooooh, is that why you’re flirting with me? Cause I remind you of your students?
: That’s not-
scene mayafestival17
: Wait, how did you know I’m a teacher? I don’t remember telling you that.
: Uhhhhhhh...hahahah!
: Two melons coming right up!
: I don’t-
scene smileex
scene tree3
scene mayafestival18
: Oh, good. You’re back.
Smile Count: 4
: Welp, there goes Ami’s college fund.
: Oh, please. Ami’s never going to college. No one is.
: How can you even eat all of this?
: I’m a growing girl.
: Or at least I would be if it weren’t for the whole time loop thing.
: I guess I’m just doomed to be eternally hungry.
: So, what did you bring me?
if amifingered == True:
: Something I think you’re going to be very happy about.
Thankfully, one of the vendors saw me struggling to carry an entire buffet’s worth of food and let me borrow a shopping cart they were using to store extra ingredients.
And I’m glad they did- because there is no way I would have been able to carry two large melons in addition to the variety of hot dishes I got.
scene mayafestival19
: Happy birthday, Maya.
: Ah! Melon!
: Two melons.
: Two melons!
scene mayafestival20
: Where in the world did you even find those? I asked every single vendor I bought from if anyone here was selling any and they all said no.
: Some weird girl was selling them. She had other shapes, too. And a...melon waitlist or something?
scene mayafestival21
: Was there really a booth like that here?...
: I had no idea.
: We’ll have to stop again before we leave.
scene mayafestival18
: Anyway, what else? I already know I’m saving the melons for last.
else:
Thankfully, one of the vendors saw me struggling to carry an entire buffet’s worth of food and let me borrow a shopping cart they were using to store extra ingredients.
And I’m glad they did- because there is no way I would have been able to carry all of this without some form of transportation.
: There’s...croquettes...taiyaki...some weird potato-on-a-stick thing...whatever this is...some other things I don’t know the name of...and a live squid.
scene mayafestival21
: What am I supposed to do with a live squid?
: I don’t know. I just blindly pointed at stuff from every booth and I guess I pointed at a live squid at some point.
: Can you go, like...kill it or something?
: Asking me for my credit card is one thing. But asking me to kill? You’re better than this, Maya.
: Am I? Because I’m pretty sure I’ve asked you to kill Noriko on several occasions and, if anything, I think I’d prefer to keep the squid alive if I had to choose between the two of them.
: I can’t wait until the day you two make up and start being friends. It’s going to be so sweet.
scene mayafestival22
: Ew, stop. At least wait until I finish eating to start saying stuff like that.
: Maya, there is so much food here that it is going to take you the rest of the festival to eat it all even if you manage to eat at your normal breakneck pace.
scene mayafestival23
: Do not underestimate my love for food.
: Festivals are to me what the dorm rooms of [teenage]girls are to you- a place where I can be free. Where my hunger can never be sated.
: I don’t know. My hunger is normally sated after half an hour or so. Sometimes, even less.
scene mayafestival24
: Why do you say things like this to me?
: Because I know you won’t think any less of me.
: I literally can not think any less of you.
: Yeah, exactly.
: Itadakimasu.
scene black
One by one, Maya tears into each plate and-
Well, I guess tear probably isn’t the right word since she somehow manages to look graceful even while consuming more than some villages do in an entire week.
But she eats everything without lessening her pace even once.
The sun begins to set as she does so, and the air begins to turn a bit colder- but that’s to be expected since it is technically still winter.
Sure, the two of us were gifted a relatively warm day by Mother Nature, but only until it was time for her to go out and party with her other cougar friends.
As Maya eats, well, everything- I slowly pick at a bowl of ramen that, at least to my unrefined palate, doesn’t compare much to what Tsuneyo makes.
But it’s warm enough to battle the encroaching cold and gives me something to do while waiting for the first stage of Maya’s favorite day of the year to end.
if amifingered == True:
scene mayafestival25
Just as she said she would, Maya saves the watermelon for dessert.
And yes, she did finish everything- including the remainder of my ramen which, despite my worsening hunger, I was not able to finish.
I recall her saying in the past that she doesn’t like being watched while she eats and, this isn’t me being weird or...fetishy, but I’m glad she seemingly abandoned that insecurity today.
There’s something oddly satisfying about seeing a girl so far detached from joy being enveloped by it that I can’t help but feel a little warmer inside.
Maybe that’s why I couldn’t finish my food.
I was already warm enough.
: Enjoying yourself?
scene mayafestival26
: A bit.
Smile Count: 5
: And you?
: For now. I’m sure that will change once I look at my credit card statement.
: At least Ami will still have a home when your house is repossessed.
: So, what’s the next phase of your game plan now that you’ve eaten from roughly every stand at this festival?
: Hmm...
: Have you changed your stance on goldfish at all in the last hour or so?
: I can’t say I have.
: Then I suppose it would be best to avoid Kingyo-Sukui. Or any other games for that matter since you’re horrible at them and I don’t want any of the prizes.
: Pretty sure that just leaves more food, then.
: Don’t forget what day it is. We still need to visit a shrine and pay our respects for the year or god might kill us. That seems like a thing he would do.
: God sounds like an asshole.
: You’re just realizing that now?
: Nope. Just reinforcing the belief with some help from you.
: I guess we can get our fortunes while we’re there too. That seems like another...festivaly thing to do.
: Not necessary.
: I draw the same one every time.
scene black
We collect our garbage, dropping everything off at a nearby receptacle.
The squid (Still alive, albeit just barely) is left there as well- clinging to life atop a stack of dirty plates.
It covers its body in a variety of sauces, seasoning itself before death, in a desperate attempt to seek out water and prolong its unappreciated existence.
Neither of us have the heart to kill it, but we have the heart to watch it die.
And that must count for something.
$ maya_love += 1
$ mayafestival2 = True
Maya’s affection has increased to [maya_love]!
jump mayafestival3
